subject.title: Backup: add encrypted snapshot backup flow

question: Should OpenClaw core sponsor this folder-backed encrypted backup snapshot flow as a native backup surface, or should core stay limited to local export/verify while off-machine/scheduled backup lives in ClawHub/plugins?
rationale: The PR adds new core CLI and openclaw.json config surface around destructive restore and secret-bearing backups, so implementation quality alone cannot decide the product boundary.

options.title: Sponsor native backup after hardening
options.body: Continue this direction only after rebasing onto current main, resolving the security findings, preserving existing archive hardening, and supplying real backup run/list/restore proof.

options.title: Keep core narrow
options.body: Keep current backup export/verify in core and ask folder-backed/off-machine snapshot workflows to ship as a ClawHub skill, plugin, or companion package unless a missing core API is identified.

options.title: Split the roadmap
options.body: Use the open backup issues to stage per-agent, migration, cloud, and restore-drill work separately instead of landing one large backup surface at once.

recommendation.title: Sponsor native backup after hardening
recommendation.body: Continue this direction only after rebasing onto current main, resolving the security findings, preserving existing archive hardening, and supplying real backup run/list/restore proof.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent backup tests/docs/refactors plus broad repository routing history make steipete the best available product-boundary owner from the observed history.
